submitter: bugs_open/410 lane — content-loss residual round. The parent round (correlation c8385154-17b4-43f5-94b2-41f552f43867, APPROVED r1 2026-08-26) shipped ScanShortfall + the strict refusal in loadStoredSections and STATED this residual rather than fixing it: `_ = json.Unmarshal(cdJSON, &s.contentData)` keeps the row and EMPTIES its content on a decode failure, so offered == kept and the count guard cannot see it. This submission closes that stated residual at the worked site, by the same design rule the approved round argued.
rationale: The residual is a second silent-loss class in the SAME loop the approved round fixed, on the content axis instead of the row axis: a decode failure used to keep the section row with a nil/empty contentData, the rerender would 'succeed', and save_page_sections then replaces the page's rows WHOLESALE (`DELETE FROM page_components WHERE page_id = $1`) — so the stored content_data that failed to decode is DESTROYED and replaced by the emptied render. Destruction, not degradation: identical to the argument the council approved for the row axis. The open question the residual comment posed ('may an unparseable section render as an empty one?') was answered by MEASUREMENT before deciding, per the estate rule that a blast-radius claim is a query, not an argument: content_data is jsonb (syntactic corruption cannot be stored), so the only reachable decode failure is a non-object value — and 0 of 2,751 non-NULL content_data values fleet-wide are non-objects [MEASURED 2026-08-31: SELECT jsonb_typeof(content_data), count(*) FROM page_components GROUP BY 1 → object 2751, NULL 56]. The refusal is therefore unreachable on every row the database currently holds; it exists for the first writer that changes that. The boundary is deliberately NOT stricter than the parse: 55 loadable rows carry SQL NULL content_data today and load as nil-map sections (a live, legitimate population), and jsonb `null` decodes to the same nil map without error — both stay loadable, and a test pins that boundary so a future 'require an object outright' edit must argue with the census. MECHANISM: reuse, not addition — on decode failure, Warn (naming the page_component id and cause) and drop the row, so the EXISTING ScanShortfall refuses the whole load with its established error shape. One refusal path, no new error literal, and the approved round's mutation tests extend naturally: mutation A (restore `_ =`) is killed by exactly the new test; mutation B (delete ScanShortfall) is killed by all three refusal tests. Both classifier layers (Go ratchet + pattern-check.py twin) verified unchanged: 207 sites / 127 files, 0 disagreements, rerender file still 0 unmarked.

plan.summary: Three edits, one mechanism: turn the stated content-loss swallow in loadStoredSections into a dropped row so the existing ScanShortfall guard refuses; pin both sides of the new boundary with tests (non-object refuses; SQL-NULL and jsonb-null stay loadable); and correct the ratchet header's blind-spot bullet so it stops describing the closed site as open while keeping the CLASS stated as uncovered.

edits.rationale: `_ = json.Unmarshal(cdJSON, &s.contentData)` becomes: on error, Warn with the page_component id and drop the row (continue), so the existing trailing ScanShortfall refuses. The replacing comment carries the dated census (0 of 2,751 non-object; 55 SQL-NULL loadable) and states why the guard is exactly as strict as the parse and no stricter.

The first poisons content_data with a JSON array (the only shape jsonb can store that the struct cannot accept) and requires the refusal to name the shortfall ('kept 1 of 2'). The second pins the legitimate nil-content population — SQL NULL and jsonb `null` both load as nil-map sections — so an over-strict future edit fails here first. Header now names both mutations and requires running both: a guard proven by one can still be dead on the other axis.

The destruction seam, verbatim [platform/orchestration/actions/save_page_sections_action.go, symbol area executeSavePageSections]: `DELETE FROM page_components WHERE page_id = $1` — the loader's result replaces the stored rows wholesale, which is why partial-or-emptied results are destruction, not degradation.

Zero arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, or jsonb nulls. Disconfirmable: one non-object row would have shown here and forced the graded/allow decision instead.

Classifier parity after the edit [2026-08-31]: Go ratchet green; Python twin: disagreements 0, 207 sites / 127 files unchanged, rerender file 0 unmarked sites. plan.risks: (1) A refusal added to the fleet's busiest rerender path. Measured unreachable on every row the database currently holds (0 of 2,751 non-object), so the change is behaviour-neutral on today's estate and converts a FUTURE silent content-emptying into a loud rerender failure. (2) Over-strictness against legitimate nil-content sections was the real hazard — 55 live rows — and is excluded by construction (SQL NULL never enters the branch; jsonb null decodes without error) and pinned by TestLoadStoredSections_NullContentDataStaysLoadable. (3) The refusal reuses ScanShortfall's error text, which says 'lost to scan failures' — a content decode failure will read as a scan shortfall in the refusal line. Accepted deliberately: the per-row Warn immediately above it names the true cause and the row id, and a second error literal would split one refusal concept into two shapes the RUNBOOK and probes would both have to know. (4) Not architecture-scope on the RFC_022/2026-07-29 tests: unexported function, single caller, no new vocabulary, no change to what any shared mechanism guarantees — it extends an already-approved refusal to a sibling axis inside the same private loader.
